gp.heading: Gross Profit
gp.text: Gross profit for the quarter increased by $1.4 million, or 13.6%, compared to the same period in 2025. Gross margin percentage for the quarter ended September 30 , 2026 increased 350 basis points compared to the prior-year quarter, primarily driven by sales growth, pricing changes, and tariff refunds received in the quarter which represented about 270 basis points of the 350 basis points of the margin improvement. The Company’s estimates of overhead allocation and the timing of inventory receipts may also have a temporary impact on gross margin percentage fluctuations from quarter to quarter.

oi.text: For the nine months ended September 30 , 2026, cash used in operations was $2.8 million, driven by net income from operations of $1.1 million, non-cash expense of $5.1 million, including depreciation, amortization, and stock-based compensation; offset by an increase in inventory of $4.5 million, a decrease in operating lease liabilities of $3.7 million, a decrease in accrued expenses of $0.3 million, an increase in prepaid expenses of $0.2 million, an increase in tax payments of $0.2 million, and a decrease in accounts payable trade of $0.1 million. Cash used in investing activities was $1.4 million mainly for purchases of property and equipment for new stores and investment in software for our new loyalty program. Cash used in financing activities was $6.2 million, primarily for dividend payments and withheld shares used as taxes at vesting for the employees. These activities, together with the effect of exchange rate changes of less than $0.1 million, resulted in a net decrease in cash of $10.4 million.

opex.heading: Operating expenses
opex.text: Operating expenses for the quarter increased by $0.1 million or 1.4% compared to the corresponding prior year period, primarily as a result of an increase in employee benefits compared to prior year of $0.1 million, an increase in salaries of $0.1 million, an increase in selling expenses of $0.1 million, an increase of depreciation of $0.1 million; offset by a reduction in property tax of $0.1 million, and a reduction of rent of $0.2 million.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Our effective income tax rate for the three months ended September 30 , 2026 and September 30 , 2025 was 17.7% and 26.2%, respectively. Our effective tax rate differs from the federal statutory rate primarily due to U.S. state income tax expense, expenses that are non-deductible for tax purposes, and any change in estimates in our valuation allowance associated with our deferred tax assets.

net sales.heading: Net Sales
net sales.text: Consolidated net sales for the quarter ended September 30 , 2026 increased by $1.3 million or a 7.3% increase compared to the same period in the prior year period. We believe the increase was mainly due to our sales campaign and improved allocation of the correct product mix in our stores during those sales periods and better execution in stores and in our E-Com channels. The improved sales is also due in part to closure of our distribution operations for at least six weeks during the third quarter of 2025 due to the relocation of our corporate offices. We also saw marginal improvement in our non-traditional sales such as classes and other community engagements.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Not only can customers purchase leather, related accessories and supplies necessary to complete their projects from a single source, but many of our store associates are also leathercrafters themselves and can provide suggestions and advice on our customers’ projects.
In general, our 10 largest suppliers account for approximately 55% of our inventory purchases, and we had one supplier in 2025 who represented about 12% of our purchases.

We anticipate that our financial performance will depend on a number of factors, including consumer preferences, the strength and protection of our brand, the introduction of new products, and the success of our business strategy.
Our success depends on our ability to anticipate and respond in a timely manner to changing customer demands and preferences for leather and leathercraft-related items.
We depend on the guidance of our senior management team and other key employees who have significant experience and expertise in our industry and our operations.
Our ability to meet the needs of our customers and our retail stores and e-commerce sites depends on the proper operation of these centers.
Our success depends on the continued protection of our trademarks and other proprietary intellectual property rights.
